match.reason: The bank's Young people's health point covers several linked youth issues and where young people live, while this point asks students to study one issue across each health dimension and its data trends, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

rejected.title: A youth health focus
card: A youth health focus means studying one issue in depth, such as mental health or body image, rather than youth health in general.
One issue can affect every dimension of health: physical, social, emotional, mental and spiritual. The effect on each dimension can be described separately.
Data show trends, which are patterns over time. A trend may show an issue becoming more common, less common or staying about the same.
Looking at the dimensions and the trends together gives a fuller picture of how the issue affects young people.
rejected.remember: Study one issue closely: its effect on each dimension of health, and its trend over time.

a.q: A student studies body image in young people. They describe how it can affect friendships, mood and eating habits. What does this show?
opts: Its effect on several dimensions of health
Its trend in the data over several years
A comparison of two different youth issues
Its effect on the physical dimension only
a.why: Friendships are social, mood is emotional and eating habits are physical, so the student is describing effects on several dimensions. No data over time are used, so this is not a trend. Only one issue is studied, and more than one dimension is covered.
a.clue: Match friendships, mood and eating to the dimensions of health.

b.q: Data show that the share of Victorian teenagers reporting high psychological distress has risen over ten years. What does this describe?
opts: A trend in the data for a youth health issue
An effect on the social dimension of health
A protective factor for a youth health issue
A comparison between two youth health issues
b.why: A rise over ten years is a pattern over time, which is a trend. Psychological distress mainly relates to the mental dimension, and the data say nothing about social effects. The figures also do not describe a protective factor.
b.clue: Which word describes a pattern over time?

version.title: A youth health focus
card: A youth health focus means studying one issue in depth, such as mental health or body image, rather than youth health in general.
One issue can affect each dimension of health: physical, social, emotional, mental and spiritual. Poor mental health, for example, can affect sleep (physical) and time with friends (social).
Data show trends, which are patterns over time. A trend shows whether an issue is becoming more common, less common or staying about the same.
Together, the dimensions show how the issue affects young people's lives, and the trends show whether it is growing or easing.
version.remember: Pick one issue: trace its effects on each dimension, then check its trend in the data.

a.q: A student studying body image notes it can lead to skipping meals, avoiding friends and feeling ashamed. What is the student describing?
opts: The issue's effects across dimensions of health
The issue's trend in the data over many years
The causes of the issue in young people's lives
The issue's effect on one dimension of health
a.why: Skipping meals is physical, avoiding friends is social and feeling ashamed is emotional, so the student is describing effects across several dimensions. Nothing here is measured over time, so it is not a trend.
a.clue: Sort each effect into a dimension of health.

b.q: Survey figures show the share of young Victorians with high psychological distress has risen over ten years. What does this tell a student about the issue?
opts: How common it is becoming over time
How it affects each dimension of health
What protects young people from it
How much it costs to treat each year
b.why: A change in a figure over ten years is a trend: it shows whether the issue is becoming more or less common. The figures say nothing about its effect on each dimension or its cost.
b.clue: Ten years of figures show a pattern over time.

a.best: The issue's effects across dimensions of health

b.best: How common it is becoming over time

check.summary: No problems found. Marked mental-health because the examples and question b are about psychological distress, and question a mentions skipping meals over body image.
